questions.question: What is Harrison Ford’s character named in Blade Runner?
questions.note: A blade runner in 2019 Los Angeles. Whether he is a replicant is a fight the movie never fully settles.

questions.question: Who directed Blade Runner (1982)?
questions.note: Scott also made Alien. Villeneuve directed the 2017 sequel.

questions.question: Blade Runner is loosely based on a novel by which writer?
questions.note: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? (1968). The film keeps the bounty-hunter plot and dumps most of the pet-sheep religion.

questions.question: In Blade Runner, what is Deckard hired to do to replicants?
questions.note: Cop talk for killing them. Bryant gives him four names. Ford plays it tired.

questions.question: In Roy Batty’s dying speech, what does he say is lost “like tears in rain”?
questions.note: “All those moments will be lost in time, like tears in rain.” Hauer trimmed and rewrote the speech.

questions.question: In Blade Runner, Deckard falls for Rachael. What does she not know?
choices: That she can fly a spinner
questions.note: Her memories are implants. Deckard still runs the Voight-Kampff on her.

questions.question: What is the name of the empathy test used to spot replicants?
questions.note: A machine, a blinking light, and questions about a calfskin wallet. Deckard runs it on Rachael.

questions.question: In Blade Runner 2049, where has Deckard been hiding for decades?
questions.note: Ford is older, bearded, and not glad to be found.

questions.question: Who directed Blade Runner 2049?
questions.note: Scott produced. Villeneuve also made Arrival and Dune.

questions.question: In what year was the original Blade Runner released?
questions.note: It flopped, then became a cult film. Several cuts exist. Trivia nights usually mean the 1982 theatrical or the later Final Cut.
